tools.name: get_device
tools.description: Details for one device. Pick sections to keep the answer small: summary (identity, address, rate, latency, clock, subscription problems), channels (custom rx and tx channel names by number; channels still on factory names are listed as number ranges), subscriptions (only receive channels that have a route, with its status; a receive channel absent here is unsubscribed), network (interfaces and redundancy), availability (which operations are writable and why not), flows (transmit and receive flows), or full for the raw record.

device.description: Device name, server name, or inventory ID as returned by list_devices.

tools.name: get_device_diagnostics

device.description: Device name, server name, or inventory ID as returned by list_devices.

fields.description: Top-level field names from get_device full.

tools.name: get_event_journal
tools.description: Recent monitoring events, newest first. Repeated observations are grouped by default; filter by device or kind, page with before_sequence, or request debug detail.

before_sequence.description: Return older events with sequence below this value.

collapse_repeats.description: Group repeated observations of the same event target; set false for every event.

device.description: Device name, server name, or inventory ID as returned by list_devices.

detail.description: Debug includes complete forensic event records.

kind.description: Only events of this kind, for example receiver_flow_latency_high.

tools.name: get_external_flows

tools.name: get_host_audio

It reads this server's computer unless host names another one, such as studio-pc. Pick a section; client narrows connections and ports to one JACK client.

client.description: A JACK client name, such as system or jack_out.

host.description: Another computer running netaudio, such as studio-pc; defaults to this server's computer.

tools.name: get_issues
tools.description: Problems detected on the network, grouped by kind and device, worst first. A failing route group names the transmitting device behind each channel. Devices that are off the network and routes waiting for them are not problems and are left out; get_routing with status waiting lists those routes, and naming an off device here shows its last report. Defaults to open issues; set state to resolved or all for history. Filter by device and page with limit; debug lists every issue separately.

device.description: Device name, server name, or inventory ID as returned by list_devices.

tools.name: get_metering_status
tools.description: Whether detailed metering is available and which devices are being metered.

tools.name: get_network_overview
tools.description: One compact snapshot of the devices on the network, clock leaders, problems and Dante Domain Manager state. Devices that are off the network are not problems and are left out; list_devices shows them with when they were last seen. Its answer field is a one-sentence reply to say first. Use focused tools for channels, routes or forensic detail.

tools.name: get_routing
tools.description: All configured receive routes across the network, including unresolved ones, grouped by receiving device. Each line reads 'rx number rx label ← tx channel on tx device'; multicast and self routes are marked, and failing routes give the reason. Channel numbers and labels both work in routing calls. Filter by receiving device, receive channel, or status.

device.description: Device name, server name, or inventory ID as returned by list_devices.

status.description: waiting selects routes whose transmitting device is off the network; those are not problems.

tools.name: get_server_info
tools.description: This netaudio server's host, version and start time.

tools.name: get_signal_levels
tools.description: Whether audio is present. Without a device: for each device, the channels carrying signal with their dBFS level and how many are silent. With a device: the rx and tx channels with signal and their level, and the silent ones by name or number range. Devices with detailed metering are sampled on request. points measures named places anywhere in the chain instead: JACK ports, PulseAudio inputs, outputs and applications, Shure channels or Dante channels. Debug includes every channel and the raw meter codes. over_last_seconds, ending_at or listen_seconds report the recorded levels over a period instead of one sample, which is what to use for sound that comes and goes.

device.description: Device name, server name, or inventory ID as returned by list_devices.

points.description: Places to measure, such as system:capture_1, default input, Discord or Wireless receiver ch1; put another computer's name first for its points, such as studio-pc default input.

over_last_seconds.description: Summarize the levels recorded over this many seconds instead of sampling once: how many seconds had signal, the loudest moment, when signal was last heard and a peak timeline. Use it for sound that comes and goes, such as someone talking on a call. Levels are kept per second for 15 minutes and per minute for 24 hours.

ending_at.description: End of that period as an ISO time, such as 2026-10-02T23:00 for last night (local time unless it has an offset or Z); defaults to now.

listen_seconds.description: Wait this many seconds, then summarize what was heard during them.

tools.name: set_subscriptions
tools.description: Set or clear any number of routes across any number of devices in one call. The server groups routes by receiving device and sends them in the largest batches each device accepts (16 per request for direct Dante control, 32 for newer firmware and managed devices), running devices in parallel. Give tx_device and tx_channel to route audio, or omit both to clear the receive channel. Prefer this over subscribe and unsubscribe for more than one route. The reply lists every route with ok true or an error.

tools.name: trace_signal
tools.description: Follow audio through the whole chain from any point: Shure wireless channels, Dante channels and routes, this computer's sound cards, JACK ports and connections, and PulseAudio inputs, outputs and application streams, on this computer and on other computers running netaudio. Lists upstream and downstream steps with bounded level observations and identifies measured transitions to silence. Internal application routing is labeled as inferred. Separate hosts and batches have separate capture windows; unavailable levels remain unknown. Use it to answer why something can't be heard. Its answer field is a one-sentence reply to say first; the rest is detail.

point.description: Where to start: a Shure channel (Wireless receiver ch1), a Dante device (every routed channel, such as Stagebox), a Dante channel (Soundcard rx 1), a JACK port or alias (system:capture_1), a PulseAudio input or output (jack_in, default input), an application (Discord), or a TV, which traces the output of the computer the TV is showing when that is known. The user's own words work too (studio laptop, wireless mic), matching names loosely, including devices that are off the network. Points on this server's computer need no prefix; put another computer's name first for its points, such as studio-pc default input.

levels.description: Measure levels at each step; about one second.

resources.tool_description: Every known device keyed by its name: product, address, online state, management (and DDM domain), sample rate, latency, channel counts, route count and any failing routes. A device that is off the network shows only its product and when it was last seen; forget_device removes ones that no longer matter. Any tool's device argument takes these names. Use get_device for channels, routes, network and operation availability.

resources.name: Event journal
resources.description: Recent monitoring events: latency, late packets, issue lifecycle and configuration changes.
resources.tool_description: Recent monitoring events, newest first. Repeated observations are grouped by default; filter by device or kind, page with before_sequence, or request debug detail.

before_sequence.description: Return older events with sequence below this value.

collapse_repeats.description: Group repeated observations of the same event target; set false for every event.

device.description: Device name, server name, or inventory ID as returned by list_devices.

detail.description: Debug includes complete forensic event records.

kind.description: Only events of this kind, for example receiver_flow_latency_high.

resources.name: External AES67 streams
resources.description: AES67 and RTP streams announced on the network by SAP.

resources.name: Issues
resources.description: Open and recently resolved problems detected on the network, with suggested remediation.
resources.tool_description: Problems detected on the network, grouped by kind and device, worst first. A failing route group names the transmitting device behind each channel. Devices that are off the network and routes waiting for them are not problems and are left out; get_routing with status waiting lists those routes, and naming an off device here shows its last report. Defaults to open issues; set state to resolved or all for history. Filter by device and page with limit; debug lists every issue separately.

device.description: Device name, server name, or inventory ID as returned by list_devices.

resources.name: Signal levels
resources.description: Latest signal level per channel for devices that are being metered.
resources.tool_description: Whether audio is present. Without a device: for each device, the channels carrying signal with their dBFS level and how many are silent. With a device: the rx and tx channels with signal and their level, and the silent ones by name or number range. Devices with detailed metering are sampled on request. points measures named places anywhere in the chain instead: JACK ports, PulseAudio inputs, outputs and applications, Shure channels or Dante channels. Debug includes every channel and the raw meter codes. over_last_seconds, ending_at or listen_seconds report the recorded levels over a period instead of one sample, which is what to use for sound that comes and goes.

device.description: Device name, server name, or inventory ID as returned by list_devices.

points.description: Places to measure, such as system:capture_1, default input, Discord or Wireless receiver ch1; put another computer's name first for its points, such as studio-pc default input.

over_last_seconds.description: Summarize the levels recorded over this many seconds instead of sampling once: how many seconds had signal, the loudest moment, when signal was last heard and a peak timeline. Use it for sound that comes and goes, such as someone talking on a call. Levels are kept per second for 15 minutes and per minute for 24 hours.

ending_at.description: End of that period as an ISO time, such as 2026-10-02T23:00 for last night (local time unless it has an offset or Z); defaults to now.

listen_seconds.description: Wait this many seconds, then summarize what was heard during them.
